note: PaulDz's six Roman way types (issue #2, 2026-08-18), ordered largest to smallest, with the band each occupies. A theme's way is DERIVED from its verse count by minVerses — never hand-tagged — so the mapping can be re-derived, argued with, and moved by changing a threshold. The order and the band edges are our proposal, awaiting PaulDz; his own list is grouped 3/3 (main streets, then small ways) and is not internally ranked.
status: proposed — not yet confirmed by PaulDz
rankedBy: verse count (exact); Greek word count (apportioned, an estimate) is a corroborating check only

types.label: Via
types.desc: The widest, grandest street; colonnades, triumphal arches, processions, and the great sewer running beneath.

types.label: Vicus
types.desc: Bustling and stone-paved, lined with apartment blocks and shops that spill into the road; crossed on raised stepping stones.

types.label: Clivus
types.desc: A steep climbing road to the temples and palaces; paving grooved for traction, heavy gutters that roar in the rain.

types.label: Semita
types.desc: A raised stone walkway beside a greater street, set above the traffic on a heavy kerb. The pedestrian safe zone.

types.label: Angiportus
types.desc: A cramped unpaved lane between tall blocks, dark even at noon; avoided at night.

types.label: Ambitus
types.desc: Two to three feet between adjacent buildings, required by law as a firebreak and for repairs; used by builders, not travellers.
